request.spec:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export tree people (CSV)" button that downloads everyone in the sheet's whole tree as a CSV file. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

The file starts with the header `sheet,name,grade,due-total`. Then come this sheet's people in list order, then the people of the tree's other sheets, ordered by sheet id. Retired people are included, and each due-total is the same figure the person's row shows.

The change is one new front-end file, `src/main/frontend/features/people/tree-export.slot.tsx`, with the button's `data-testid` set to `export-tree`. The server and stored data didn't need changes. An existing `/api/sheets/{sheet}/tree` endpoint already returns the current sheet followed by the rest of its tree by id. The tree search uses the same endpoint, and I copied its way of working out each sheet's figures.

When you press the button, it fetches that list of sheets, waits until every sheet's data has been freshly read from the store, then builds and downloads the file. The button is disabled while this runs.

There's one difference from the tree search: the export follows the screen's as-of date if one is set, while the search always shows figures as they stand now. None of the tests use an as-of date with the export, so that choice isn't tested.
